title: 2-D Shapes: Sides, Corners, Curved, Opposite and Parallel Sides
seo_title: Year 2 2-D Shapes Worksheets: Sides, Corners and Parallel Sides (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Recognise, compare and classify shapes, referencing the number of sides and using spatial terms such as “opposite”, “parallel”, “curved” and “straight”
meta_desc: Free Year 2 maths worksheets on 2-D shapes: name triangles, squares, rectangles, pentagons, hexagons, octagons, circles and ovals, count sides and corners, spot curved and straight sides, find opposite and parallel sides, and sort shapes. 100 questions with an answer key, following the Australian Curriculum.
key_big: Count the sides to name a 2-D shape. Turning a shape does not change its name.
key_sub: Sides can be straight or curved. Opposite sides are across from each other. Parallel sides stay the same distance apart and never meet.
body_html:
Name a shape by its sides

A 2-D shape is flat. Count its sides to find its name. A corner is where two sides meet. Corners are also called vertices.

ShapeSidesCorners
Circle1 curved side (same width all the way round)0
Oval1 curved side (longer than it is wide)0
Triangle33
Square4 (all the same length)4
Rectangle4 (2 long, 2 short)4
Pentagon55
Hexagon66
Octagon88

Turning a shape does not change its name. The sides do not have to be the same length.

Example 1

A shape has 5 straight sides. Two sides are longer than the others. What is it?

Count the sides: 5. The lengths do not matter.

Answer: a pentagon

To count sides, put your finger on one side. Count each side as you go round, until you are back where you started. Count the corners that point in too.

Curved and straight sides

A straight side does not bend. A curved side bends. Some shapes have both.

Example 2

A semicircle is half a circle. How many sides does it have?

It has 1 curved side and 1 straight side. 1 + 1 = 2.

Answer: 2 sides

Opposite and parallel sides

Opposite sides are across the shape from each other, not next to each other. Parallel lines stay the same distance apart. They never meet, even if you make them longer.

Example 3

The top of a rectangle is 9 cm long. How long is the bottom?

The bottom is opposite the top. Opposite sides of a rectangle are the same length.

Answer: 9 cm

Sort and classify

We can sort shapes by the number of sides, by curved or straight sides, or by parallel sides. To find the odd one out, look for the one thing that three shapes share and the fourth does not.

Example 4

Which is the odd one out: square, rectangle, triangle, hexagon?

The square, rectangle and hexagon all have parallel sides. The triangle has none.

Answer: triangle

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Calling a turned square a “diamond”Check the sides: 4 sides the same length and 4 square corners make a square
Calling an oval a circleA circle is the same width all the way round. An oval is longer one way
Missing a side, or counting one twiceStart at one side, keep your finger on the shape and stop when you get back
Counting only the points of a starCount the corners that point in too
Thinking parallel lines must go acrossSlanted and up-and-down lines can be parallel too
Saying a rectangle has 4 pairs of parallel sidesA pair is 2 sides. A rectangle has 2 pairs

faq.q: What 2-D shapes do Year 2 students learn in Australia?
faq.a: Year 2 students name circles, ovals, triangles, squares, rectangles, pentagons, hexagons and octagons. They compare and sort them by the number of sides, curved or straight sides, and opposite and parallel sides (Australian Curriculum AC9M2SP01).

faq.q: What does parallel mean in Year 2 maths?
faq.a: Parallel lines stay the same distance apart and never meet, like the two rails of a train track. A rectangle has 2 pairs of parallel sides.

faq.q: Is a turned square called a diamond?
faq.a: No. A square turned on its corner is still a square, because it still has 4 equal sides and 4 square corners. “Diamond” is an everyday word, not a maths name.

faq.q: What is the difference between a circle and an oval?
faq.a: Both have 1 curved side and no corners. A circle is the same width all the way round; an oval is longer than it is wide, like a footy ground.

items.q: What is this shape called?
items.e: It has 4 straight sides and 4 square corners. 2 sides are long and 2 are short. It is a rectangle.

items.q: What shape is this?
items.e: Count the sides: 5 straight sides. It is a pentagon.
It is round and the same width all the way round. It has no corners. It is a circle.

items.q: Name this shape.
items.e: It has 4 straight sides and 4 square corners. 2 sides are long and 2 are short. It is a rectangle. Turning a shape does not change its name.

items.q: What is this shape called?
items.e: Count the sides: 8 straight sides. It is an octagon.
It is round with no corners, but it is longer than it is wide. It is an oval, not a circle.

items.q: What is this shape called?
items.e: It has 3 straight sides and 3 corners. It is a triangle. Turning a shape does not change its name.

items.q: Name this shape.
items.e: It has 4 straight sides that are all the same length, and 4 square corners. It is a square.

items.q: Which shape is a hexagon?
items.e: A has 6 straight sides, so it is a hexagon. The other shapes have 5, 8 and 4 sides.

items.q: What is this shape called?
items.e: Count the sides: 5 straight sides. It is a pentagon. The sides do not have to be the same length.

items.q: Which shape is a pentagon?
items.e: D has 5 straight sides, so it is a pentagon. The sides do not have to be the same length.
C is round with no corners, and it is longer than it is wide. That makes it an oval. The circle is the same width all the way round.

items.q: What shape is this?
items.e: It has 4 straight sides that are all the same length, and 4 square corners. It is a square. It is only turned. “Diamond” is not its maths name.

items.q: Name this shape.
items.e: Count the sides: 8 straight sides. It is an octagon. Count the short sides at the corners too.

items.q: A shape has 4 straight sides. 2 sides are long and 2 are short. It has 4 square corners. What is it?
items.e: 4 sides and 4 square corners, with 2 long sides and 2 short sides: a rectangle. A square has 4 sides the same length.

items.q: Name this shape.
items.e: Count the sides: 6 straight sides. It is a hexagon.

items.q: What shape is this?
items.e: Count the sides: 6 straight sides. It is a hexagon. The sides do not have to be the same length.

items.q: A shape has 6 straight sides. What is it called?
items.e: 6 sides make a hexagon. 5 sides make a pentagon. 8 sides make an octagon.

items.q: Which shape is a square?
items.e: B has 4 sides that are all the same length and 4 square corners. It is a square that is turned. The other shape with 4 equal sides has no square corners, so it is not a square.

items.q: What shape is this?
items.e: It has 3 straight sides and 3 corners. It is a triangle.
An oval has 1 curved side. The ends are round, not pointed, so there are no corners. 2 counts the ends.

items.q: Which shape has the most sides?
items.e: C has 8 sides. The others have 6, 5 and 4 sides. 8 is the most.

items.q: How many sides does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one side. Count each side as you go round, until you get back to the start: 6 sides. Count the corners that point in too.

items.q: How many corners does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one corner. Count each corner as you go round, until you get back to the start: 4 corners.

items.q: How many corners does this star have?
items.e: There are 5 corners that point out and 5 corners that point in. 5 + 5 = 10 corners. 5 only counts the points.

items.q: Which shape has 4 corners?
items.e: D has 4 corners. It is a square that is turned. The others have 5, 3 and 6 corners.

items.q: A shape has 5 corners. How many straight sides does it have?
items.e: A shape with straight sides has the same number of sides as corners. 5 corners means 5 sides.

items.q: How many corners does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one corner. Count each corner as you go round, until you get back to the start: 8 corners. Count the small corners too.
A circle has 1 curved side and no corners. So it has 0 corners.

items.q: How many corners does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one corner. Count each corner as you go round, until you get back to the start: 3 corners.

items.q: How many more sides does an octagon have than a hexagon?
items.e: An octagon has 8 sides. A hexagon has 6 sides. 8 − 6 = 2 more. 14 adds them instead.

items.q: How many sides does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one side. Count each side as you go round, until you get back to the start: 7 sides. Count the corners that point in too.

items.q: How many sides does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one side. Count each side as you go round, until you get back to the start: 4 sides.

items.q: How many sides does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one side. Count each side as you go round, until you get back to the start: 5 sides.

items.q: How many sides does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one side. Count each side as you go round, until you get back to the start: 4 sides.

items.q: How many corners does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one corner. Count each corner as you go round, until you get back to the start: 5 corners.

items.q: How many sides does this shape have?
items.e: Each arm of the cross has 3 sides. There are 4 arms. 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 12 sides. 4 only counts the arms.

items.q: Which shape has 6 corners?
items.e: B has 6 corners. Count the corners that point in too. The others have 5, 7 and 4 corners.

items.q: How many corners does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one corner. Count each corner as you go round, until you get back to the start: 4 corners.

items.q: How many sides does this shape have?
items.e: Put your finger on one side. Count each side as you go round, until you get back to the start: 6 sides. Count the corners that point in too.
This shape has 1 straight side and 1 curved side. So it has 1 straight side.
This shape has 3 straight sides and 1 curved side. So it has 3 straight sides.

items.q: Which shape has 1 curved side and no straight sides?
items.e: A circle has 1 curved side all the way round. A semicircle also has 1 straight side.
This shape has 0 straight sides and 1 curved side. So it has 1 curved side.
A corner is where two sides meet at a point. This shape has 2 corners. At the top, the straight sides join the curve smoothly, so there is no corner there.
This shape has 2 straight sides and 2 curved sides. So it has 2 straight sides.
This shape has 3 straight sides and 1 curved side. So it has 1 curved side.
Both sides of D bend. The others have straight sides.
A has 1 curved side and 1 straight side. The circle has only a curved side. The square and pentagon have only straight sides.

items.q: Which shape has only straight sides?
items.e: A triangle has 3 straight sides. A circle and an oval have a curved side. A semicircle has a curved side and a straight side.
A corner is where two sides meet at a point. This shape has 2 corners. They are at the two ends of the straight side.

items.q: How many curved sides does this shape have?
items.e: This shape has 2 straight sides and 1 curved side. So it has 1 curved side.
This shape has 2 straight sides and 1 curved side. So it has 2 straight sides.
This shape has 0 straight sides and 2 curved sides. So it has 2 curved sides.

items.q: A semicircle is half a circle. How many sides does it have altogether?
items.e: It has 1 curved side and 1 straight side. 1 + 1 = 2 sides. 1 forgets the straight side.
This shape has 2 straight sides and 2 curved sides. So it has 2 curved sides.
This shape has 0 straight sides and 2 curved sides. So it has 0 straight sides. Every side bends.
A corner is where two sides meet at a point. This shape has 3 corners.
B is a hexagon. All 6 of its sides are straight. The others have a curved side.
This shape has 1 straight side and 1 curved side. So it has 1 curved side.

items.q: Which shape has no parallel sides?
items.e: A is a triangle. Its sides all slant towards each other, so none are parallel. The rectangle, hexagon and square all have opposite sides that are parallel.

items.q: Which pair of lines is parallel?
items.e: The lines in A stay the same distance apart. They will never meet, even if you make them longer.

items.q: How many pairs of parallel sides does this shape have?
items.e: Only the top and the bottom are parallel. The two slanted sides would meet if you made them longer. So there is 1 pair.

items.q: In which shape are the two red sides parallel?
items.e: In D the red sides are opposite each other and point the same way. They are parallel. The red sides in the other shapes slant towards each other.

items.q: Which side is opposite side A?
items.e: Side D is right across the shape from side A. Opposite sides are across from each other, not next to each other. In this hexagon they are also parallel.

items.q: How many pairs of parallel sides does this triangle have?
items.e: Every side of a triangle slants towards the other two. If you make the sides longer, they all meet. So there are 0 pairs.

items.q: Which pair of lines is parallel?
items.e: The lines in B go straight up and down and stay the same distance apart. So they are parallel.

items.q: This is a rectangle. How long is the right side?
items.e: The right side is opposite the left side. Opposite sides of a rectangle are the same length. So it is 3 cm.

items.q: In which shape are the two red sides parallel?
items.e: In C the red sides are opposite each other and stay the same distance apart. They are parallel. In the other shapes the red sides would meet if you made them longer.

items.q: How many pairs of opposite sides does this square have?
items.e: Side A is opposite side C. Side B is opposite side D. That is 2 pairs. 4 counts every side, not pairs.

items.q: How many pairs of parallel sides does this octagon have?
items.e: Each side has an opposite side that is parallel to it. 8 sides make 4 pairs. 8 counts every side.

items.q: Which side is opposite side B?
items.e: Side F is right across the shape from side B. Opposite sides are across from each other, not next to each other. In this octagon they are also parallel.

items.q: Which of these has parallel lines?
c: the hands of a clock at 3 o’clock
the two rails of a train track
items.e: The two rails of a train track stay the same distance apart, so they are parallel. The lines in a V meet, and the lines in an X cross.

items.q: How many pairs of parallel sides does this hexagon have?
items.e: Each side has an opposite side that is parallel to it. 6 sides make 3 pairs. 6 counts every side.

items.q: Which pair of lines is NOT parallel?
items.e: In C the lines get closer together. If you make them longer, they will meet. So they are not parallel.

items.q: What are parallel lines?
c: lines that stay the same distance apart
lines that meet at a corner
items.e: Parallel lines stay the same distance apart. They never meet, even if you make them longer.

items.q: Which pair of lines is parallel?
items.e: The lines in D slant the same way and stay the same distance apart. Slanted lines can be parallel too.

items.q: This is a rectangle. How long is the bottom side?
items.e: The bottom side is opposite the top side. Opposite sides of a rectangle are the same length. So it is 9 cm.

items.q: Which side is opposite side C?
items.e: Side F is right across the shape from side C. Opposite sides are across from each other, not next to each other. In this hexagon they are also parallel.

items.q: How many pairs of parallel sides does this rectangle have?
items.e: The top and bottom are parallel. The left and right sides are parallel. That is 2 pairs. 4 counts every side.

items.q: I have 4 square corners. My opposite sides are parallel. My sides are not all the same length. What am I?
items.e: A rectangle has 4 square corners and 2 pairs of parallel sides. A square would have all 4 sides the same length.
It is round with no corners, and it is longer than it is wide. It is an oval. That is why we call a footy ground “the oval”.

items.q: Which shape is the odd one out?
items.e: C is a triangle. It has no parallel sides. The other three shapes all have opposite sides that are parallel.

items.q: Kai makes a hexagon with paddle-pop sticks. He uses 1 stick for each side. How many sticks does he use?
items.e: A hexagon has 6 sides. 1 stick for each side means 6 sticks.

items.q: Which shape is the odd one out?
items.e: B has 5 sides. The other three shapes all have 4 sides.

items.q: William has 5 triangles, 4 squares and 3 circles. How many of the shapes have only straight sides?
items.e: Triangles and squares have only straight sides. 5 + 4 = 9. Circles have a curved side, so do not count them.

items.q: Mei draws 3 triangles. How many corners is that altogether?
items.e: Each triangle has 3 corners. 3 + 3 + 3 = 9 corners.

items.q: Isla sorts shapes. Group 1: square, triangle, hexagon. Group 2: circle, oval. What is the sorting rule?
items.e: Group 1 shapes have only straight sides. Group 2 shapes have a curved side. So the rule is straight or curved.

items.q: I have 5 straight sides and 5 corners. What shape am I?
items.e: 5 sides and 5 corners make a pentagon.

items.q: A cricket pitch has 2 long sides, 2 short sides and 4 square corners. What shape is it?
items.e: 4 straight sides and 4 square corners, with 2 long and 2 short sides: a rectangle. A square has 4 sides the same length.

items.q: A STOP sign is this shape. How many sides does it have?
items.e: A STOP sign is an octagon. An octagon has 8 sides and 8 corners.

items.q: Ava makes 2 triangles and 1 square with paddle-pop sticks. Each side is 1 stick. How many sticks does she use?
items.e: Each triangle has 3 sides and a square has 4. 3 + 3 + 4 = 10 sticks. 7 forgets one triangle.

items.q: Mia cuts the 4 corners off a square piece of paper with straight cuts. How many sides does the new shape have?
items.e: Each cut makes 1 new short side. The 4 old sides are still there. 4 + 4 = 8 sides. The new shape is an octagon.

items.q: Matilda draws a hexagon. She colours 2 sides red. How many sides are not red?
items.e: A hexagon has 6 sides. 6 − 2 = 4 sides are not red. 8 adds instead of taking away.

items.q: I have no corners. I am longer than I am wide. What shape am I?
items.e: No corners means only a curved side. Longer than wide means it is an oval. A circle is the same width all the way round.
D has a curved side. The other three shapes have only straight sides.

items.q: Which shape is the odd one out: triangle, square, circle, hexagon?
items.e: A circle has a curved side and no corners. The others have straight sides and corners.

items.q: A GIVE WAY sign is this shape. What shape is it?
items.e: It has 3 straight sides and 3 corners, so it is a triangle. It points down, but it is still a triangle.

items.q: Liam cuts a rectangle along the red line, from corner to corner. What 2 shapes does he get?
items.e: Each piece has 3 straight sides and 3 corners. So he gets 2 triangles.

items.q: The Australian 50c coin has 12 straight sides. How many corners does it have?
items.e: A shape with straight sides has the same number of corners as sides. 12 sides means 12 corners. It is not round, so 0 is wrong.
